slides.subtitle: Four EPC2361 per switch: DPT and load-test boards, 1200 V / 300 kW SPB inverter
slides.author: Enes Ayaz, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, October 2026

slides.title: Design flow

rows: 1200 V, 300 kW, M ≤ 1.15, PMSM cos φ = 0.9 → 228 A_{rms} per leg
100–650 V GaN survey, absolute and per volt → 100 V GaN, EPC2361 (Kelvin pad)
V_{m} + L·di/dt ≤ 90 V for 0.5 / 1 nH, even N → 75 V, N = 16
loop of one cell + LTspice at 0.5 / 1 nH → ≤ 80 A per device
loss, T_{j}, V_{DS} vs n → 4 EPC2361 per switch
≥ 50 kHz; 3 % ripple → 20 × 22 µF 2220 + 10 × 1 µF bypass per cell
one 2EDF7275K per pair (star, Kelvin) → building block of two cells
two pairs, one DC pair, one AC output → DPT board and load-test board
two isolated supplies + Zener bias, UFCS per cell (DPT), U.FL V_{GS}, MMCX V_{DS}, HO 250-S
legs share the 75 V bus → laminated PCB busbar; 3D level and 16-level stack
fast Q3D set on the final boards and the busbar; fab files

slides.title: Design inputs

rows: V_{DS} ≤ 90 V at nominal bus (100 V part)

paras: SPB: N three-phase submodules in series on the DC side, each feeding one winding set of the machine
V_{m} = 1200 V / N per submodule; each submodule = 3 legs on one DC link

slides.title: Phase current follows from the inputs

paras: Each of the 3N legs delivers P/3N at V_{ph} = M·V_{m}/(2√2):
I_{rms} = P / (3 · M·V_{bus}/(2√2) · cos φ)
N·V_{m} = V_{bus}: the phase current does !!not!! depend on N
**228 A_{rms} per leg**, 322 A peak (cos φ = 0.9)
DC current per leg 83 A; series DC chain 250 A
Losses in this deck are for cos φ = 0.9; the PMSM operating point is confirmed with the machine design

slides.title: Voltage class: why 100 V GaN

paras: (a) At fixed bus voltage and phase current the minimum semiconductor loss scales with √(R_{DS(on)}·C_{oss,tr}): the 100 V GaN parts have the lowest product

(b) Per volt of blocking capability: 100 V GaN has the lowest R_{DS(on)}/V_{DS,max} (EPC2361 7.5 µΩ/V, 3–30× below 200–650 V) at a higher C_{oss}/V; conduction dominates here (12.4 W vs 4–5 W switching per leg, step 5)
(c) Best device per class: 100 V needs more submodules but the fewest devices per switch and the smallest voltage step → **EPC2361**, 100 V, 0.75 mΩ typ, 3 × 5 mm, top-side cooling

slides.title: EPC2361: key data and the Kelvin source

paras: Kelvin pad 2 next to the gate: the gate loop returns at the die, the source stripes and vias (L_{S}) stay in the power loop only ⇒ no L_{S}·di/dt feedback into v_{GS}
Low threshold and −4 V limit: gate bump and negative bias need care (step 7)
Top of the package at !!source potential!!: the thermal interface must insulate

slides.title: Submodule voltage from L·di/dt

paras: Peak stress v̂_{DS} = V_{m} + L_{loop}·di/dt ≤ 90 V; turn-on di/dt (gate-charge model, R_{g,on} 2 Ω): 25 / 33 / 50 A/ns at 60 / 80 / 120 A per device
At 80 A per device: V_{m} ≤ **73 V** with 0.5 nH, only 57 V with 1 nH ⇒ the loop must stay near 0.5 nH (or the turn-on is slowed); N even (symmetric winding sets): 16 → 75 V

items.text: V_{m} = 75 V, N = 16; layout target 0.5 nH per cell

slides.title: Why not lower: every submodule costs parts and loss

paras: Phase current is fixed by P, V_{bus}, M, cos φ, not by N
Each submodule carries the full phase current ⇒ conduction loss, transistors, drivers and supplies scale with N
60 V (N = 20): +25 % parts and conduction loss
Overshoot margin rechecked on the final boards (Q3D, step 11)

slides.title: Power loop of one cell: copper, bypass ESL and shunt

paras: Q3D of the final boards (cell band): loop = copper of the vertical loop over 0.1 mm (vias, pads) + bypass ESL/n (+ UFCS 120 pH on the DPT board)
Copper alone: 0.35 nH (load) / 0.47 nH (DPT, shunt path); with 6 + 4 bypass 0805 per cell: **0.41 / 0.65 nH**
Beyond ≈ 4 bypass parts per cell the number hardly matters; part: 1 µF 100 V X7S 0805 next to the drains

items.text: Design value L_{loop} = 0.5 nH per cell; 1 nH as the pessimistic bound

slides.title: One EPC2361 per switch: how fast and how much overshoot

paras: LTspice half bridge at 75 V, lumped loop 0.5 / 1 nH, 1.7 nH gate loop, 2 Ω on / 0 Ω off, 4 A / 8 A driver
(b, c) A larger loop lowers E_{on} (the loop takes L·di/dt of the voltage while the current rises) but raises E_{off} and the overshoot; turn-on di/dt is set by the driver (≈ 45 A/ns)
(d) Conduction per device at 100 °C: 4.0 / 7.2 / 16.1 W at 60 / 80 / 120 A_{rms}; one device would carry 322 A peak ⇒ **current per device ≤ 80 A**

slides.title: Switching frequency: losses, DC-link capacitors, current ripple

paras: (a) n = 4: 99.77 / 99.71 / 99.61 % at 20 / 50 / 100 kHz; (b) the voltage ripple sets the 2220 count (20 per leg at 50 kHz), ripple current needs only 7; (c) winding ripple Δi_{pp} = V_{m}/(4 L_{σ} f_{sw}) depends on the machine

items.text: f_{sw} ≥ 50 kHz (higher allowed by the machine); the DC link is sized for 50 kHz

slides.title: DC-link sizing for a three-phase level

paras: One 75 V level = three legs on one bus (SVPWM, M = 1.15, cos φ = 0.9)
Balanced three-phase: no 2f ripple; capacitor RMS current 85 A per level (≈ 28 A per leg)
Per switching period the bank supplies the difference between the cell current and its average: ΔV_{pp} = ΔQ / C

items.text: ΔV_{pp} ≤ 3 % (2.25 V) at 50 kHz ⇒ 127 µF **effective** per leg board ⇒ 20 × 22 µF 2220

slides.title: Capacitor selection: effective capacitance at 75 V

paras: DC bias at 75 V from the manufacturers' characteristic data (TDK, Murata): 100 V class-II MLCCs keep only 15–29 %
TDK C5750X7S2A226M280KB (2220, 22 µF): highest C per part and per area (0.22 µF/mm²), 2.8 mΩ, 4.5 A for +10 K
Checks: 2.8 mm height under the heatsink spreader; 2220 flex cracking ⇒ away from the board edge and holes

items.text: Bank: **20 × TDK C5750X7S2A226M280KB** per leg (2 rows), 127 µF effective, 1.4 A ripple per part

slides.title: Bypass capacitors: how many and how large

paras: **Bypass** (1 µF 0805 at the drains) supplies the edge, **bank** the f_{sw} ripple; per cell 81 A:
di/dt → number: L_{Cu} + ESL/n ≈ 0.5 nH ⇒ n ≥ 4
Hand-over to the bank through L_{b}: C_{bp} ≥ L_{b}(ΔI/ΔV)² !!sets the value!!
L_{b} from Q3D: (pending)
0805 1 µF 100 V X7S keeps only **18 %** at 75 V (TDK data): 0.18 µF per part
dip for 6 / 10 per cell: (pending bank model)

items.text: 10 × 1 µF 0805 per cell: 6 on top at the drains + 4 on the bottom, identical in all cells

slides.title: DC link of one leg board

paras: Ripple at 50 kHz with the three legs of a level sharing: **2.1 V (2.9 %)**
Leg alone (DPT, back-to-back test without the busbar): ≈ 2× higher, acceptable for the lab tests
Bank ≥ 10 × bypass (127 vs 7 µF eff.): fulfilled
Row A leaves the board centre free for the DC terminal pins

slides.title: Can one driver drive all four?
slides.section: 7  Gate drive: from 4 devices to a building block

paras: Why E_{on} per transistor rises with n per channel: the n gate capacitances (n × 3.6 nF C_{iss}) charge through one driver output (4 A source, 0.85 Ω) and a longer shared gate trace ⇒ v_{GS} rises n× slower ⇒ lower di/dt and dv/dt at turn-on ⇒ longer V–I overlap: **+16 / +31 / +60 %** E_{on} for 3 / 4 / 6
(b) Extra gate-loop inductance of the longer tree raises the gate bump; (a) peak sink current 12–14 A for 4–6 devices exceeds the 8 A rating
(c) One channel per device is symmetric but needs 4 channels and supplies per switch

slides.title: Driver arrangement for 1 … 4 EPC2361 per switch

paras: One dual-channel driver (HS + LS) between two cells: both gate loops equal and with their own Kelvin return (design value ≈ 1.7 nH; extracted on the routed board: step 11)
n = 3 breaks the symmetry (pair + single)
n = 4: two pairs, two drivers, one star per pair ⇒ the building block of two point-symmetric cells

items.text: 2 × EPC2361 per driver channel; 4 per switch = two pairs = two drivers

slides.title: Gate driver selection: why the 2EDF7275K

paras: A pair needs ≈ 2 × 3.6 nF: 4 A / 8 A drives it at the single-device speed; the 1.5 A / 3 A half-bridge driver does not
Two isolated outputs in one 5 × 5 mm LGA: HS and LS of the same pair from one IC, ≤ 3 ns channel mismatch
Floating outputs: each output gets its own supply split (5.1 V Zener on, −1.9 V off) for the bump margin (next)

items.text: Data: Infineon / TI product pages and datasheets (2EDF7275K, 1EDF5673K, LMG1210); check the current revision.

slides.title: Why symmetry: what sets the current sharing

items.text: Star gate network with Kelvin returns, one driver channel per pair, point-symmetric cells

slides.title: Gate bump and negative off-voltage

paras: **Bump:** when the other device of the leg turns on, the off device sees dv/dt; C_{GD}·dv/dt flows through its gate loop and lifts v_{GS} by ≈ Q_{GD}/C_{GS} ≈ 1.06 V
Independent of load current and bus voltage (top b, c); close to the 0.8 V minimum threshold ⇒ shoot-through risk
**Negative off-voltage** shifts the whole bump down: −1 V ⇒ peak ≈ 0 V; extra C_{GS} divides it further (bottom)
Cost: reverse conduction in the dead time at V_{SD} + |V_{off}|; off-state ringing must stay above the −4 V limit
Implemented: V_{GS,off} = −(V_{ISO} − 5.1 V) = **−1.9 V** (V_{ISO} = 7 V), set with the extracted gate loop (step 11): bump ≤ −0.5 V, ringing ≈ −3.4 V

slides.title: Two driver pairs on one switch node: driver skew

paras: The four switch nodes are joined in copper; L_{x} = inductance between the switch nodes of the two driver pairs
If driver 2 switches Δt later, pair 1 takes ΔI ≈ V_{m}·Δt / L_{x} until pair 2 follows
Q3D (fast lx model, final boards): L_{x} = **6.77 nH** (HS on) / **5.44 nH** (LS on) on the load board, 4.91 / 2.68 nH on the DPT board
⇒ **≈ 14 A per ns of skew** (load board)

slides.title: Gate supplies: two isolated supplies, Zener split

paras: One external isolated supply for all HS drivers and one for all LS drivers; each splits per driver through a WE-CNSW common-mode choke
5.1 V Zener VDD–S and 150 Ω bias resistor S–VEE (Karakaya, METU 2020, Fig. 4.1): V_{GS,on} = +5.1 V, V_{GS,off} = −(V_{ISO} − 5.1 V)
V_{ISO} = 7.0 V ⇒ −1.9 V off (bump mitigation, inside the −4 V limit); island decoupling 1 µF + 4.7 µF per rail

slides.title: Driver block: input filters, turn-on / turn-off paths, star

paras: Per block a 2×5 control header (each signal next to its return); common-mode chokes on 12 V, DIS and NTC, none on PWM_H / PWM_L (no extra delay or LC ringing with the 100 pF input filter; removed after the PWM review)
47 Ω / 100 pF input filters, 10 k pull-downs, R_{ON} 1.5 Ω (shared by the pair), R_{OFF} 0 Ω + Schottky, R_{G} 0.5 Ω per transistor ⇒ R_{g,on} = 3.5 Ω per device

slides.title: Three legs on one 75 V bus: what the bus must do

paras: The switching edge closes on each board (bypass + bank); the bus only carries the f_{sw} ripple between the leg banks
Sharing needs ωL_{bus} ≪ 1/(ωC): at 50 kHz and ≈ 127 µF eff. per leg L ≪ 80 nH ⇒ **target ≤ 5 nH leg to leg**
DC: 250 A stack current enters the level, 83 A per leg
All-MLCC banks joined by nH copper form a high-Q resonator ⇒ damping footprints

paras: Extracted gate network: Q3D copper + 0.4 nH per 0603 resistor body + 1 nH D_{OFF}; UFCS 120 pH as its own inductor
